key_insight: Shield synthesis is reframed from a runtime safety tool into a design-time analysis method that certifies whether a network topology and specification are defensible.
engineering_relevance: For security architecture, the paper offers a formal way to identify which network designs can be defended, where the safe regions are, and how resilient they are under adaptive attackers.
method: Compile defender and attacker temporal-logic specifications into automata.
Build a constrained two-player safety game and compute attractors/winning regions.
Extract a defensibility verdict plus topology-level metrics and a shield-based fingerprint.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a what-if analysis showing that small architectural changes can strongly affect operational outcomes even when formal safety margins remain nearly unchanged.
watch_item: Results depend on the chosen specifications and game abstraction, so the defensibility verdict may not fully capture real-world attacker behavior or model mismatch.
paper_title: Beyond Runtime Enforcement: Shield Synthesis as Defensibility Analysis for Adversarial Networks
